comparison: Perfect agreement on core mirrored organization findings (C2, C33-C37). Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical methods, adequate sample size, and consistent effects across brain regions. All three peer reviewers accept these findings as solid and straightforward.

Complete agreement on null findings (C6, C52, C68). Both evaluations find SUPPORTED that atypical organization does not impair task performance. OpenEval notes missing statistical details for null results, but peer reviewers accept the finding without challenge as consistent with the study's focus on organizational patterns.

Both evaluations rate claims about compelling evidence for Causal hypothesis (C63, C64, C110) as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval questions the 'first demonstration' claim and notes substantial individual variability contradicts 'compelling evidence.' Peer reviewers similarly emphasize individual variability supports Statistical hypothesis and accept conclusions with important caveats.

Agreement on UNCERTAIN rating for bilingualism confound (C67, C121). OpenEval notes speculation due to insufficient monolinguals but argues bilingual status equivalence between groups mitigates concern. Peer reviewers treat this as a significant methodological limitation affecting generalizability, with stronger emphasis on the problem.

Both find individual-level variability data (C38-C42) SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes 55.8% ambilateral pattern introduces complexity but authors appropriately acknowledge this. Peer reviewers explicitly discuss this variability (including C3, C43-C44) as important qualification supporting Statistical hypothesis at individual level.

OpenEval evaluates voxel-wise overlap in ambilateral subgroup (C3, C43-C44) as SUPPORTED, noting frequent functional overlap in IFC. Peer reviewers incorporate these same claims into their discussion of individual variability, treating them as part of the evidence for Statistical hypothesis.

Both find interhemispheric functional connectivity findings (C4, C48, C90) SUPPORTED. OpenEval rates broader set of connectivity/structural claims as SUPPORTED but raises concerns about modest effect sizes and lack of multiple comparison correction. Peer reviewers accept connectivity findings without challenge.

Both find corpus callosum structural findings (C5, C45-C47, C89) SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes modest effect sizes and correlational nature. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge white matter volume associations and present them as consistent with corpus callosum hypothesis without raising methodological concerns.

Divergent evaluations of schizotypy correlations (C7, C59, C91). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to multiple comparison concerns, small effect sizes, and lack of theoretical justification. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, acknowledging correlational nature but not challenging validity of the association.

Divergent evaluations of AQ correlations (C8, C61, C92). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN with concerns about multiple comparisons and differential patterns lacking justification. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, accepting the differential pattern (language LI with AQ, inhibition LI with SPQ) without question.

Divergent evaluations of reading accuracy correlations (C9, C53-C57, C93). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to multiple comparison issues and small effect sizes, though notes reading findings are more consistent. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, describing findings as 'interesting evidence' without raising statistical concerns.

OpenEval finds subcortical involvement claim (C65) SUPPORTED based on STN and thalamic findings extending lateralization beyond cortical structures. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses this subcortical extension claim.

OpenEval rates theoretical framework reconciling individual variability (C78-C82) as UNCERTAIN, noting speculation without empirical support and potentially incorrect 'failed development' interpretation. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses this specific theoretical framework.

OpenEval finds sample characteristics and group equivalence (C113-C121) SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical tests and adequate sample size, noting limitation to non-right-handed individuals. Peer reviewers reference C121 in bilingualism discussion but do not provide separate evaluation of sample characteristics.

OpenEval rates summary/conclusion statements (C102-C112) as UNCERTAIN, arguing 'compelling evidence' claim overstates case given correlational nature, modest effects, and individual variability. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these integrated conclusion claims separately from other evaluations.
